questions.discovery_question: Walk through your AP process step by step — from invoice receipt to payment. Who touches it at each stage?
questions.branch_answer:
We process between 13,000 and 16,000 invoices a month across just shy of 1,100 communities. AP is centralized in an AP specialist group; the decentralized part is the approval process, which the AP group does not perform. Ideally all invoices go directly to the Avid Strongroom AP lockbox, but we still receive some at the branch and some sent directly to managers, who email or upload them into Strongroom. The digital invoice image is indexed to the property and to the vendor, then routed to the manager, who approves it and provides the GL coding based on the budget or the board's approval. It then goes to the accountant (or the AP team) for a secondary check — a sanity check of those items plus confirmation that there are enough funds to release the payment. It then goes to a final release stage, a bulk release to pay, performed by Melanie, Janet or Peter. Alternative processes add a board approval step at the very beginning or the very end, for fewer than 50 properties. After final release, Strongroom sends checks to its print queue and check printers, or to its Avid Pay back-end for vendors enrolled in electronic methods.

questions.discovery_question: Do you have dollar limits that require Board Member or Branch Executive approval before paying an invoice? What are the thresholds and who approves?
questions.branch_answer:
In Strongroom there are no dollar thresholds — board involvement in approval is all or nothing. Boards typically ask to approve items over $5,000, and we have to tell them it is all or nothing: they are either part of the approval process for everything or none of it. Fewer than 50 properties total have a board in the approval chain, and Strongroom can grant boards either view-only access or approval access. In Vantaca there is a threshold: a manual check request over what we believe is $50,000 has to have signature approval.

questions.discovery_question: Do you pay any vendors by ACH? If yes, how do you set up an ACH vendor and how are payments initiated?
questions.branch_answer:
We do not pay vendors any way other than check unless the vendor signs up through Avid Strongroom. The default payment method is check. Strongroom/Avid offers vendors the option to enroll for expedited payment by credit card or ACH; those agreements are between the vendor and Strongroom and CMA is not involved at all. Our system still shows the method as check; Strongroom's back-end handles the electronic payment when the invoice is approved. We can tell after the fact from the payment itself — an Avid electronic payment drafts out of the association bank account almost immediately and shows as Avid Pay in the history list. The one exception we set up ourselves is bank draft / auto draft, used for vendors such as utilities, where we set the default method to bank draft so it does not produce a check. We do not collect vendor bank information.

questions.discovery_question: If there is not enough money in an association's bank account to pay a vendor, what happens? Who decides what gets paid and in what order?
questions.branch_answer:
It does not happen that often. We default to paying utilities and insurance first. Beyond that it goes back to the community manager (CAM) to decide what needs to be paid or whether to hold it until funds come in. For the roughly 50 properties where the board is in the approval process, the manager would discuss it with the board. Funding sufficiency is also checked by the accountant at the secondary approval stage before release, and accounting will send an invoice back to the manager for funding issues or for the wrong bank account being selected.

questions.discovery_question: How do you view the payment history for a vendor or a specific invoice? Can you add notes or comments to an invoice record?
questions.branch_answer:
Managers can see from their view in Strongroom what has been paid previously for a vendor, which is how they check for possible duplicates where there is no unique invoice number. Invoices carry notes: there are notes that go onto the check stub and notes that are internal only. The internal notes carry the accountant's comment when an invoice is kicked back, and managers use the notes section to explain items such as paying 50% as a deposit or paying from a statement with no original invoice, so we know to release it. Kicked-back items appear in the manager's Strongroom queue, and Strongroom lets managers enable or disable email alerts. questions.discovery_question: How do you detect and prevent duplicate vendor invoices across all entry channels before payment is released?

questions.discovery_question: What controls/checks happen between the AP system, the bank, and fraud mitigation measures (e.g., Positive Pay) before money leaves the account?
questions.branch_answer:
We use positive pay, and for electronic payments we require dual authorization. Once a payment imports into Vantaca, Vantaca sends the positive pay file to the bank; positive pay runs a day behind, so whatever posts today appears in positive pay tomorrow. The only time we have to intercede is when something not on the positive pay file tries to clear, in which case the bank sends us an exception notice. Positive pay is currently set up only for Citizens — Enterprise is not set up yet, with a goal of before the end of the year; Enterprise is a secondary bank holding mostly money market accounts for reserves with very few transactions, and for those we get a bank notification to authorize release of the payment. For advanced payment methods such as wire transfers, approval goes beyond the accounting staff and can only be performed by one of the authorized signers on the accounts, and we require the wiring instructions plus the name and phone number of someone at the bank to verify those instructions. Segregation of duties: the manager who approves and the AP team who pays cannot set up the vendor, and a manager or accountant cannot both approve and release. What positive pay does not catch is a check stolen from the mail with the signature forged — same payee, same amount, same check number — which we only find out about when the vendor calls to say they have not been paid.

How do you track which vendors are 1099-eligible and ensure you have their TIN or EIN on file before year-end? Is this managed inside your accounting system or outside it?
questions.branch_answer:
Eligibility is flagged at vendor setup: other than kicking off the year-end action item, the only place we have input is during vendor setup, where there is a box to check — 1099 or not 1099. Required documents at setup are the W-9 and the certificate of insurance, and the tax ID comes from the W-9; we do not collect any other vendor information. It is managed inside Vantaca. TIN coverage is incomplete and payment is not blocked without it — the system allows paying a vendor with no tax information, and Melanie noted "there's plenty of that". Known gaps: boards sometimes insist on a particular contractor who will not provide insurance or a W-9, in which case we make the board sign a waiver so the decision is theirs; we do not chase utilities, attorneys or insurance companies for W-9s since they would not receive a 1099 anyway; and legacy vendors from before Strongroom compliance, or inherited from acquired management companies, have missing tax information. A further issue is that a board member who both performs a service and claims a reimbursement needs two vendor records set up, because Vantaca should allow only one — Melanie believes Vantaca can exclude items from the 1099 but was unsure how that gets caught at year-end.

questions.dimension: Positive Pay file generation & bank transmission
questions.discovery_question: Does your branch use Positive Pay with your bank? If so, how is the Positive Pay file generated after each check run and transmitted to the bank?
questions.branch_answer:
Yes, we use positive pay. Once a payment imports into Vantaca from Avid Strongroom, Vantaca sends the positive pay file to the bank. It is a day behind — whatever posts today appears in positive pay tomorrow. When something not on the positive pay file tries to clear, the bank sends us an exception notice and that is the only point at which we have to intercede. For items with no matching invoice, such as a recurring ACH, we can set up a standing ACH authorization rule approving that payee for that amount so it clears rather than raising an exception. Coverage is not complete: positive pay is set up for Citizens only. Enterprise Bank is not set up yet, with the goal of getting it done before the end of the year; Enterprise is a secondary bank with mostly money market reserve accounts and very few transactions, and for those we get a bank notification to authorize release. Positive pay does not catch a check stolen from the mail and forged with the same payee, amount and check number.

questions.branch_answer:
Partly, and it depends on the system. In Avid Strongroom there is no dollar threshold: board participation in approval is all or nothing, and although boards typically ask to approve items over $5,000 we have to tell them they are either in the approval process for everything or none of it. In Vantaca there is a threshold — a manual check request over what Melanie believed to be $50,000 has to have signature approval. Separately, and not threshold-based, for electronic payments we require dual authorization, and wire transfers require approval beyond the accounting staff by one of the authorized signers on the account. Every invoice already passes two approvals regardless of amount (manager, then accountant), and approval and release are segregated — a manager or accountant cannot do both; only accounting manager and above can.

Signatures are stored digitally in Vantaca, accessible only to an administrator, and the bank module only allows selecting which signature block applies to a bank account, tied to the selecting user. Voids are handled through the accountant via an inquiry, or a manual check request in Vantaca, and the reconciliation of checks issued against checks clearing happens through the monthly bank reconciliation, where aged items trigger a stop-payment-and-reissue inquiry. No check stock ordering or inventory control process, and no distinct void log, was described. [PARTIAL]

questions.discovery_question: When a stop payment is needed on an issued check, walk me through the steps — who initiates it, how is the bank notified, and how is the outstanding item cleared in the GL?
questions.branch_answer:
Stop payments are triggered by aging or by a known problem. During the monthly bank reconciliation, critical items such as utilities or insurance aged about 30 days prompt an inquiry to the manager on whether to let it sit or stop payment and reissue; general AP is 90 days on the same rule. Other triggers include a check lost in the mail where the vendor must be paid today — the original payment is stopped and we cut a manual check. Initiation is by an inquiry to the accountant for an existing check, or a manual check request in Vantaca for the replacement. Sequencing matters: we have to void it in Avid Strongroom first and then cut a manual check in-house. For a regular mailed Strongroom check, though, you cannot void it in Strongroom; if you void it in Vantaca and reissue, Strongroom comes in overnight through the integration and voids the check you just reissued, because it matches on the invoice — and then positive pay flags it. Voiding and reissuing an Avid/Strongroom check also inevitably has trouble printing locally, whereas a manual check reissues cleanly, and because the same Vantaca process handles both there is no easy way to tell which is which. How the bank is notified of a stop payment was not described. [PARTIAL]
